Neovision Brackenfell Corner is a branch of Neovision, a South African network of optometry practices based in shopping centres around the country. The practice carries out comprehensive eye examinations and vision assessments, including glaucoma screening, and stocks a range of prescription eyewear, sunglasses and contact lenses to suit different budgets and lifestyles. Optometrists see patients for routine checks as well as ongoing monitoring of eye health, while dispensing staff assist with frame choices, lens upgrades and fittings.

The practice trades from Shop 14 in Brackenfell Corner Shopping Centre, at the corner of Frans Conradie Drive and Paradys Street in Brackenfell, making it an easy stop to combine with other shopping in the centre. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 2pm, suiting both weekday appointments and weekend visits for shoppers in the area.

Neovision Welgemoed is part of the Neovision optometry network, which operates practices in shopping centres across South Africa. The branch offers full eye tests to check vision and eye health, along with glaucoma screening, and a selection of designer frames, sunglasses and contact lenses for adults and children. Qualified optometrists handle consultations and prescriptions, and the in-store team helps patients choose and fit eyewear suited to their needs and budget.

Based in Welgemoed Forum at the corner of Jip de Jager and Kommissaris Street in Welgemoed, the practice serves shoppers from Welgemoed, Bellville and the surrounding northern suburbs. It keeps weekday hours from 9am to 5pm and is open on Saturdays from 9am to 2pm, giving residents a convenient option for an eye test without travelling into central Cape Town.

Nestle Purina Petcare operates a production and distribution facility in Ndabeni as part of Purina, the pet care division of the global Nestle group. Purina develops and manufactures pet food under well-known brands sold across South Africa, covering everyday dry and wet food as well as ranges formulated for specific life stages, breeds and health needs for dogs and cats. The Ndabeni site supports the manufacturing and supply chain that gets these products onto retailer shelves around the country.

As an industrial facility rather than a retail outlet, it is not set up for walk-in customers, but it plays a role in the wider pet care industry in the Western Cape through local production and logistics. It sits in Ndabeni, an established industrial node on the edge of Cape Town, within easy reach of the city's main transport routes.

New York Bagels is a dedicated bagel bakery in Zonnebloem, making its bagels the traditional way: hand-rolled, boiled and then baked, rather than simply baked like ordinary bread rolls. The bakery offers a range of bagel varieties through the day, along with fillings and spreads for those eating in or taking away, bringing a New York-style bagel shop experience to central Cape Town. Its approach focuses on the chewy crust and dense crumb associated with proper bagels, rather than a quick imitation.

The bakery trades from Harrington Street in Zonnebloem, within walking distance of the CBD and the East City precinct, and has built a following through word of mouth as much as passing trade. It opens early, from 7am on weekdays, and keeps shorter hours over the weekend, making it a popular stop for breakfast or a quick lunch.

Ocean Basket is a well-established South African seafood restaurant chain known for generous, moderately priced portions of fish, prawns, calamari and other seafood served in a relaxed, family-friendly setting. Menus typically include grilled and battered fish, platters, sushi, pasta and a children's menu, giving groups with different tastes something to choose from in one sitting. The chain has built its reputation on casual, sit-down dining rather than fine dining, with a focus on quick service and shareable dishes.

The Sea Point branch trades from St Johns Piazza on Main Road, on the first floor above street level, serving local residents and visitors to this busy stretch of the Atlantic Seaboard. It is open daily, with slightly longer hours on weekends, and offers both dine-in seating and takeaway for those who prefer to eat elsewhere.

OK MiniMark is a convenience grocery store trading from Blackberry Mall at the corner of Dennegeur and Church streets in Strandfontein. It stocks everyday essentials such as bread, dairy, snacks, drinks and household basics, giving residents a nearby option for top-up shopping without needing a full supermarket trip. The store keeps a presence on social media where shoppers can see updates, which is typical of the smaller, community-focused MiniMark format within the wider OK retail group.

Trading seven days a week from Blackberry Mall, the store is open from 7:30am to 9pm on weekdays and Saturdays, and from 8am to 8:30pm on Sundays, covering most of the day for people living nearby. Its long, consistent hours make it a reliable stop for last-minute groceries in Strandfontein.

OK Minimark Summer Greens is a neighbourhood convenience store on Summer Greens Way, serving the surrounding residential area with everyday grocery essentials. Alongside packaged goods, drinks and household items, the store runs its own in-store butchery and bakery counters, so shoppers can pick up fresh meat and freshly baked bread or rolls on the same visit rather than making separate trips. This combination of convenience-store basics with fresh counters is a common format for smaller stores trading under the OK brand.

The store is based in Summer Greens, part of the Milnerton area north of the Cape Town city centre, and is positioned to serve people living in the surrounding streets rather than drawing shoppers from further afield. Its fresh counters make it a practical choice for quick, everyday shopping close to home.

Opulence Events & Function Venue is a dedicated event space in Schaapkraal, in the Philippi Horticultural Area, set up to host weddings, parties and other private functions. The venue has built up a strong following on social media, with thousands of followers and hundreds of people having checked in after attending events there, pointing to steady use for celebrations in the southern suburbs. Its own description promotes a setting for memorable occasions, with function space that can be arranged around each booking's decor and catering.

Located on 4th Avenue off Schaap Road in Schaapkraal, the venue sits within the farming area known as the Philippi Horticultural Area, offering more space and privacy than venues closer to the city centre. It suits couples and families looking for a function venue away from the busier parts of Cape Town.

Panorama Veterinary Clinic & Specialist Centre is a veterinary practice offering both general consultations and specialist-level care, as its name suggests, for dogs, cats and other companion animals. Day-to-day services include check-ups, vaccinations and treatment of illness and injury, while the clinic's emergency service means animals needing urgent attention outside normal hours can still be seen. This round-the-clock emergency cover sets it apart from practices that only see patients during the working day.

The clinic is based on Uys Krige Drive in Panorama, a central spot that is easy to reach from surrounding northern suburbs such as Parow, Goodwood and Plattekloof. It is open Monday to Friday from 7am to 7pm and on Saturdays from 8am to 1pm, with its 24-hour emergency service available outside those times for genuine emergencies.

PEP is one of South Africa's largest clothing and homeware retail chains, known for low prices on basics such as everyday clothing, underwear, school uniforms, footwear and household items for the whole family. Stores typically also offer services such as airtime, prepaid electricity and money transfers at the till point, making them a stop for more than just shopping. The chain's model is built around keeping costs down so that essentials stay affordable for a wide range of households.

The Blue Downs branch trades from Blue Downs Shopping Centre at the corner of Hindle Road and Eerste Rivier Way, serving shoppers across Blue Downs and the surrounding Eerste River area. It opens seven days a week, including Sunday trading hours, giving customers flexibility to shop over the weekend as well as during the week.

PEP Goodwood Mall is a branch of PEP, a national discount retailer selling affordable clothing, footwear and homeware alongside everyday household essentials. The chain is built around value pricing rather than fashion-led ranges, stocking basics for babies, children and adults, along with linen, towels and small household items that cover most of a family's everyday needs. Many PEP stores also offer in-store services such as airtime and bill payments, adding convenience beyond ordinary retail.

This branch trades from Goodwood Mall at the corner of McDonald Street and Voortrekker Road in Goodwood, within one of the busier retail nodes on the southern side of Voortrekker Road. Its position inside the mall means it benefits from passing shoppers visiting the centre's other stores, and it keeps extended weekday and weekend trading hours to match.

This PEP store is part of South Africa's biggest value clothing and homeware chain by number of outlets, offering budget-friendly basics for babies, children and adults alongside linen, towels and small household goods. The chain's appeal lies in its low prices on everyday items rather than seasonal fashion, which keeps it a regular stop for families managing a tight household budget. Many branches also provide in-store services such as prepaid airtime and electricity.

The Kensington branch trades from Kensington Shopping Centre on 12th Avenue, serving the Kensington community and nearby Factreton and Maitland. It is open six days a week, closing on Sundays, with slightly shorter hours on Saturdays, making it a convenient weekday stop for residents doing their everyday shopping close to home.

Pet Plus Lakeside is a pet supply store trading from The Old Bakery at the corner of Lincoln Road and Main Road in Lakeside, part of a small Pet Plus group with other branches, including one in nearby Tokai. The store stocks pet food, treats, bedding and accessories from recognised brands for dogs, cats and other household pets, with staff able to advise on diet and general pet care. Its listing describes good prices and service, with the store open every day of the week.

Trading from The Old Bakery centre in Lakeside, the store is easily reached from Muizenberg, Kalk Bay and the surrounding False Bay suburbs. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and on weekends from 9am to 3pm, giving pet owners a nearby option for both routine supplies and last-minute needs.

Pharmacy Penlyn is an independent community pharmacy operating from inside the Shoprite store in Philippi, dispensing prescription medicines and offering general pharmacy advice to shoppers in the area. Alongside dispensing, pharmacies of this kind typically provide over-the-counter medication, basic health screening and guidance on managing chronic conditions and everyday ailments, making them a first point of contact for minor health concerns. Being based inside a supermarket means customers can collect medicine while doing their grocery shopping on the same trip.

The pharmacy trades from the Shoprite store at the corner of Lansdowne and New Eisleben Roads in Philippi, serving the surrounding residential community. Its hours are split across the week, including a midday break on Fridays, and it is open shorter hours over the weekend to fit around typical shopping patterns in the area.

Pick n Pay is one of South Africa's major supermarket chains, stocking a full grocery range that includes fresh produce, meat, bakery items, and everyday household and personal care products. Stores in the group typically combine national brands with Pick n Pay's own-label ranges, giving shoppers a mix of choice and value across most categories needed for a weekly shop. The chain is also known for its loyalty programme, which rewards regular shoppers with points and personalised offers.

This branch trades from Eden on the Bay Mall at the corner of Sir David Baird and Otto du Plessis Drives in Big Bay, Bloubergstrand, serving residents of this coastal suburb north of Cape Town. It opens from 8am to 8pm on weekdays and Saturdays, and from 9am to 8pm on Sundays, covering most of the week for local shoppers.

Pick n Pay Family is a smaller-format version of the Pick n Pay supermarket brand, designed for more compact retail spaces while still covering core grocery needs such as fresh produce, bread, dairy, frozen goods and household basics. The Family format typically focuses on everyday essentials rather than the full range found in larger Pick n Pay hypermarkets, making it suited to a quicker, more local shopping trip. It still carries a mix of national brands and Pick n Pay's own-label products.

This branch is based in The Junxion Mall at the corner of Govan Mbeki and New Eisleben Roads in Philippi East, serving the surrounding community with accessible, everyday grocery shopping. It is open from 8am to 6pm on weekdays and 9am to 5pm over weekends, giving shoppers a consistent schedule to plan around.

This Pick n Pay branch forms part of one of South Africa's largest supermarket chains, offering a full grocery range spanning fresh produce, meat, bakery goods, frozen food and household essentials under one roof. Like other stores in the group, it combines well-known national brands with Pick n Pay's own-label products, and shoppers can make use of the chain's loyalty programme for points and personalised discounts on their usual purchases.

The store trades from Richmond Corner at the corner of Plattekloof and Tygerberg Valley Roads in Richwood, Milnerton, serving residents of Richwood and the surrounding Plattekloof and Welgemoed areas. It keeps long daily hours, from 8am to 7pm on weekdays, 8am to 6pm on Saturdays and 8am to 5pm on Sundays, suiting shoppers doing a full week's groceries or a quick top-up.

Pizzayiro is a restaurant in Sitari Village Centre built around a fusion of Italian and Greek street food, best known for its wood-fired pizzas and yiros, the Greek wrap of grilled meat, salad and sauce rolled in flatbread. The menu brings together two cuisines that share a love of simple, fresh ingredients cooked quickly over flame, giving diners a choice between a classic pizza night and something a little different. It operates for both sit-down meals and takeaway orders, with delivery also available through online platforms.

The restaurant trades from Sitari Village Centre on Sundarbans Drive in Croydon, part of the Sitari Estate development near Somerset West, serving residents of the surrounding new neighbourhoods. Its position within the village centre makes it an easy dinner option for people living in or near the estate.

Quicktrip Bakery is a bakery and coffee shop trading from Quicktrip Shopping Centre on Merrydale Avenue in Portlands, Mitchells Plain. The bakery produces fresh bread, pastries and cakes on site, alongside a coffee counter, giving customers a stop for breakfast, a quick snack or a cake for a celebration without travelling further afield. Its own promotion of its baked goods and coffee offering as the core of the business is in keeping with a traditional neighbourhood bakery rather than a large chain outlet.

Based in the Quicktrip Shopping Centre, the bakery is positioned to serve the surrounding Portlands community as part of everyday errands. It opens from 9am to 7pm Monday to Saturday and from 8am to 6pm on Sundays, giving residents a long window through the week to pick up fresh baking.

Reno Spur is a branch of Spur Steak Ranches, a long-running South African family restaurant chain known for steaks, burgers, ribs and chicken wings served in a casual, sports-themed setting. Spur restaurants typically include a dedicated children's menu and play areas in many branches, making them a popular choice for family outings as well as casual meals with friends. The chain has built its identity around generous portions and a relaxed dining experience rather than fine dining.

This branch trades from Bellville Mall on Bill Bezuidenhout Avenue in Bellville, serving diners from across the northern suburbs who are shopping at or passing through the mall. It is open daily from 8am, with slightly later closing times on Fridays and Saturdays, covering breakfast through to dinner service.

Rite Price Supermarket is a neighbourhood grocery store on Hek Street in Lavender Hill, Steenberg, serving local residents with everyday food and household items. Stores of this kind typically focus on core grocery lines such as bread, dairy, packaged food, drinks and cleaning products rather than the full range found in larger supermarkets, making them a practical option for a quick, nearby shop rather than a weekly stock-up elsewhere. Independent grocers like this often compete on convenience and personal service within their immediate community.

Based in Lavender Hill, the store is positioned within walking distance for many residents of this part of Steenberg. Its hours include a midday break on weekdays and Fridays, with longer trading on Saturdays and shorter hours on Sundays, fitting around typical shopping patterns in the area.

RocoMamas is a South African burger chain known for gourmet-style burgers, loaded chicken wings and ribs, served in an informal, music-driven setting aimed at a younger crowd. Menus are built around build-your-own burger options and indulgent toppings, setting the chain apart from more traditional family restaurants, and most branches offer both dine-in seating and takeaway for customers on the go. The brand has grown into a familiar name in shopping centres across the country.

This branch trades from Okavango Crossing shopping centre on Okavango Road in Kraaifontein, serving residents of Kraaifontein and the surrounding northern suburbs. It is open from 11am daily, closing at 10pm during the week and slightly later on weekends, making it a regular option for dinner or a late lunch.

Roman's Pizza is a well-known South African pizza chain built around affordable takeaway and delivery pizza, with a menu that includes classic and specialty toppings alongside sides such as garlic bread and wings. The chain has grown a large footprint of outlets across the country by focusing on quick turnaround and value pricing rather than sit-down dining, which keeps most branches compact and geared toward collection and delivery orders.

This outlet trades from Parklands Junction at the corner of Parklands Main Road and Wood Drive in Parklands, serving residents of Parklands, Table View and the surrounding West Coast suburbs. It opens at 10am daily, closing at 9pm on weeknights and Sundays and slightly later on Fridays and Saturdays, giving customers a long window for ordering throughout the day and evening.

Rose Corner Cafe is a small corner cafe and convenience store in Bo-Kaap, the kind of neighbourhood shop that stocks everyday basics such as snacks, drinks, bread and small grocery items alongside light refreshments for customers passing by. Shops like this typically serve a mix of local residents doing quick top-up shopping and visitors exploring the area on foot, and they often stay open outside the hours of larger supermarkets nearby.

The cafe is based on Wale Street in Bo-Kaap, within a close-knit residential area on the slopes of Signal Hill above the city centre. Its corner position and small-shop format make it a convenient stop for a snack or a few grocery essentials without needing a car or a longer shopping trip.

Rosebank Progress College is an independent private secondary school formed through the merger of Rosebank House Damelin College and Progress College, bringing two established Cape Town institutions together under one roof. The school offers a mainstream secondary curriculum leading to matric, in a smaller, more personal setting than many government schools, which can suit learners who benefit from closer attention or a change from a previous school environment. Independent schools of this kind often also accommodate pupils re-entering formal schooling or needing a flexible timetable.

The college is based on Main Road in Rosebank, within reach of the southern suburbs and the Cape Town CBD. It keeps weekday hours from 8am to 5pm and is closed over weekends, in line with standard school scheduling.

Roseberry is a Chinese and sushi restaurant in Mowbray offering Asian-inspired curries and stir-fries alongside an all-you-can-eat sushi buffet, giving diners a choice between a cooked Chinese-style meal and a self-serve sushi spread in one sitting. This combination of cuisines under one roof, rather than a single-style menu, is aimed at groups with different tastes who want to eat together without compromising on what they order. The restaurant serves both diners eating in and customers collecting takeaway orders.

Based on Durban Road in Mowbray, the restaurant is positioned close to the University of Cape Town's Rondebosch-Mowbray area, drawing a mix of students, staff and local residents. It is open daily except Sundays, from late morning through to dinner, giving customers a wide window to visit.

Rouge Day Spa, based in The Old Bakery in Lakeside, offers facials, skincare treatments and massage as part of its spa menu, with options that include acne-focused facials and treatments designed specifically for men alongside the more usual relaxation-based offerings. Having both acne and men's facials listed separately from standard treatments points to a menu built to cover specific skin concerns rather than only general pampering, which broadens who the spa can realistically serve. Bookings are typically made in advance for treatment slots.

The spa trades from The Old Bakery at the corner of Main Road and Lincoln Road in Lakeside, convenient for clients from Muizenberg, Kalk Bay and the wider False Bay area. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 4pm, closing on Sundays.

Salisburys is a delicatessen and wine shop on Roodebloem Road in Woodstock, combining a deli counter with a curated wine selection under one roof. Customers can pick up deli fare such as cold meats, cheeses and prepared food alongside coffee, while also browsing wines chosen rather than simply stocked in bulk, giving the shop a more personal, specialist feel than a standard bottle store or supermarket deli counter. It suits both a quick coffee stop and slower browsing for a dinner party or gift.

The shop is based in Woodstock, an area known for its mix of independent food and design businesses close to the Cape Town city centre. It opens early on weekdays, from 7:30am to 8pm, with shorter hours over the weekend.

Sasol operates a network of fuel stations across South Africa, and this branch provides fuel and forecourt services at the corner of 5th Avenue and Voortrekker Road in Maitland. Stations in the group typically pair fuel sales with a convenience shop stocking snacks, drinks and basic motoring items, along with services such as tyre checks and car washes at larger sites, making them a stop for more than just a fill-up. Running around the clock is common for busier branches on main routes.

Positioned on Voortrekker Road, one of Cape Town's older arterial routes, the Maitland station serves commuters travelling between the city centre and the northern and eastern suburbs. Trading 24 hours a day, it gives drivers a reliable option for fuel and quick purchases at any time, including outside normal shopping hours.

Scientific Manufacturing is a family-run business established in 1971, specialising in laboratory test equipment and light-duty stainless steel engineering from its base in Killarney Gardens. Having operated under family ownership for more than five decades, the business has built up long-standing experience in designing and producing equipment for laboratory and testing applications, an area that calls for precision work rather than mass production. Its stainless steel engineering side extends this precision work into custom fabrication beyond laboratory equipment alone.

The business is based on Le Mans Avenue in Killarney Gardens, an industrial area north of Milnerton, placing it within reach of other manufacturing and engineering firms in the same part of Cape Town. It trades Monday to Thursday from 8am to 4pm and Friday from 8am to 3pm, closing over weekends.

Shoe City is a national footwear retailer selling shoes, sandals and sneakers for men, women and children across a range of budgets, from school shoes to casual and sport styles. As part of a larger retail group, the chain is able to stock a broad selection of brands and sizes, aiming to cover most everyday footwear needs for a household in one visit rather than requiring trips to multiple specialist stores. Seasonal ranges typically shift to cover school uniform shoes, summer sandals and winter boots as needed.

This branch trades from Shop L41 in Ottery Centre on New Ottery Road in Ottery East, serving shoppers from Ottery, Lotus River and the surrounding southern suburbs. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 7pm and on Saturdays from 8am to 5pm, closing on Sundays.

Shoprite is South Africa's largest supermarket chain by store count, offering a full grocery range that includes fresh produce, meat, bakery goods, frozen food and household essentials, generally positioned on value and everyday low prices. Most Shoprite stores also include an in-house bakery and butchery counter, and many offer money services such as bill payments and money transfers at dedicated counters, adding convenience beyond grocery shopping alone.

This branch trades from Airport Shopping Centre at the corner of Stellenbosch Arterial and Belhar Drive in Belhar, serving residents of Belhar and the surrounding Delft and Bellville South areas. It is open from 9am to 7pm on weekdays, 8am to 7pm on Saturdays and 8am to 5pm on Sundays, giving shoppers a wide window across the week for their grocery needs.

This Shoprite branch is part of South Africa's biggest supermarket chain, built around offering groceries at everyday low prices rather than premium ranges, covering fresh produce, meat, bakery items, frozen food and household basics under one roof. Many Shoprite stores combine this core grocery offer with in-store bakery and butchery sections, along with services such as bill payments, giving shoppers reasons to visit beyond a standard shopping list.

The store trades from Grand Central Shopping Centre at the corner of Main and Plein Street in Eerste River, serving the surrounding Eerste River community and nearby Blue Downs. It opens from 8am to 8pm on weekdays, 8am to 6pm on Saturdays and 8am to 4pm on Sundays, covering most of the week for local shoppers doing their grocery run.

SIK Liquidation Centre is a discount retailer in Elsies River Industrial, selling electronics, furniture, clothing and household goods at reduced prices rather than carrying a single category of stock. This liquidation model typically relies on buying surplus, returned or end-of-line stock and passing the savings on to customers, which means the range on the floor can shift from one visit to the next as new stock comes in. Shoppers after a specific item are generally better served checking in person than expecting a fixed, repeating stock list.

The store trades from Botha Street in Elsies River Industrial, an area known for a mix of factories, warehouses and discount retailers on the northern edge of Cape Town. It is open Monday to Friday from 8am to 5pm and over weekends from 8am to 2pm.

Simply Asia is a Thai restaurant trading from Howard Centre in Pinelands, with a menu built around stir-fries, red and green curries, noodle dishes and other Thai specialities rather than a broader pan-Asian offering. The focus on Thai cooking specifically, rather than a mixed Asian menu, points to a kitchen geared toward balancing the sweet, sour, salty and spicy flavours that define the cuisine, with dishes designed for sharing as much as individual ordering. The restaurant operates as part of a small group of Simply Asia branches trading under the same name in other centres.

Based in Howard Centre on Forest Drive in Pinelands, the restaurant serves residents of Pinelands and nearby Thornton and Pinelands North. It is open daily from late morning into the evening, with slightly shorter hours on Sundays.

Sitari Medical Centre is a multidisciplinary practice in Sitari Village Centre bringing together general doctor consultations and aesthetics treatments alongside physiotherapy and Pilates under one roof. This mix lets patients deal with everyday health concerns, work with a physiotherapist on injury recovery or mobility, and attend Pilates sessions, or book in for aesthetics treatments, without needing to visit several separate practices around the area. It is a format suited to a growing residential estate where residents want several types of care close to home.

The centre trades from Shop 38 in Sitari Village Centre on Sundarbans Drive in Croydon, within the Sitari Estate development near Somerset West. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 1pm, closing on Sundays.

Solo Factory Shop is a factory outlet in Salt River's Brickfield precinct, selling discounted kids', men's and ladies' clothing and footwear sourced from reputable retailers rather than operating as a standard retail store with fixed seasonal ranges. Factory shops of this kind typically carry overstock, past-season lines and samples at reduced prices, which means stock can vary between visits, rewarding regular shoppers who check in from time to time rather than those looking for one specific item on demand.

The shop trades from Unit 14 on Brickfield Road in Salt River, an area known for a cluster of factory outlets and wholesale clothing shops close to the Cape Town city centre. It is open Monday to Friday from 8:30am to about 4:20pm and on Saturdays until around 1:20pm, closing on Sundays.

SuperSpar is one of the larger store formats within the SPAR group, a South African supermarket brand built on independently owned and operated stores trading under a shared banner and supply network. The SuperSpar format typically carries a full grocery range, including fresh produce, meat, a bakery and household essentials, giving it more depth than smaller Spar Express or convenience-format stores in the same group. Many branches also operate an attached liquor store under the Tops brand.

This branch trades from IPIC Shopping Centre on Doordekraal Road in Kenridge, Durbanville, serving residents of Kenridge and the surrounding Durbanville suburbs. It is open daily from early morning, 7am on weekdays and Saturdays and 7:30am on Sundays, through to around 8pm, suiting both a full weekly shop and a quick top-up visit.

Southfield Superette is a small convenience store on Victoria Road in Southfield, stocking everyday groceries and household essentials for residents in the immediate area. Stores described as a superette typically sit between a small corner shop and a full supermarket, carrying a narrower range than a large grocery chain but enough variety to cover most day-to-day household needs without a special trip further afield. They tend to rely on repeat, local custom rather than drawing shoppers from across the city.

Based on Victoria Road, the store sits within Southfield, a residential suburb on Cape Town's southern side near Plumstead and Diep River. Its position on a main through-road makes it an easy stop for residents walking or driving past on their way to and from home.

SPAR is a South African supermarket brand made up of independently owned and operated stores trading under a shared name and supply network rather than a single centrally run chain. This branch, SPAR Avonwood, carries the group's usual range of groceries, fresh produce and household essentials, with the specific product mix and service shaped to some extent by the local owner-operator rather than set entirely from head office. SPAR stores often also stock a selection of ready meals and bakery items aimed at quick, everyday shopping.

The store trades from Avonwood Square at the corner of 35th Avenue and Balvenie Avenue in Elsies River, serving residents of Elsies River and the surrounding Avonwood area. Its position in the square makes it accessible to shoppers on foot as well as those arriving by car.

SPAR Brackenfell Corner trades under the SPAR banner, a South African supermarket brand made up of independently run stores that share a name, buying power and distribution network rather than being centrally owned outlets. The store stocks a full grocery range, including fresh produce, meat, bakery goods and household essentials, and like many SPAR branches keeps longer hours than some of its larger supermarket competitors, which suits shoppers needing groceries outside standard business hours.

Based in Brackenfell Corner Shopping Centre at the corner of Frans Conradie Drive and Paradys Street in Brackenfell, the store serves shoppers across Brackenfell and the surrounding northern suburbs. It trades seven days a week, including public holidays, from 7am to 8pm Monday to Saturday and from 8am to 8pm on Sundays.

This SPAR branch is part of a South African supermarket brand built on a network of independently owned stores operating under one name and supply chain, rather than a single company running every outlet directly. The Kensington store carries the group's standard grocery range, from fresh produce and bakery items to household essentials, giving local shoppers an alternative to the area's other supermarket chains for their everyday shop.

Trading from Shop 18 on 12th Avenue in Kensington Shopping Centre, the store serves the Kensington community alongside nearby Factreton and Maitland. It opens from 7:30am to 7pm on weekdays, with a midday break on Fridays between the morning and afternoon sessions, and keeps similar hours on Saturdays and shorter hours on Sundays.

SPAR Woodstock Quarter is a supermarket branch of the SPAR group, which operates as a network of independently owned stores trading under a shared brand and supply chain across South Africa. The store carries typical SPAR grocery lines, including fresh produce, bakery goods, meat and household essentials, aimed at residents and workers in and around the surrounding retail development rather than drawing shoppers from across the wider city.

Based within the Woodstock Quarter development on Sir Lowry Road, the store sits among a mix of offices, eateries and other retail close to the Cape Town CBD. It opens from 7am to 8pm on weekdays, 8am to 6pm on Saturdays, and 8am to 3pm on Sundays and public holidays, fitting around the rhythms of a mixed-use precinct.

Spec-Savers at Longbeach Mall in Noordhoek has provided optometry services since 2001, offering eye examinations, a range of eyewear and contact lens fittings from two on-site optometrists. Having two optometrists based at the branch, rather than one visiting periodically, means patients can generally be seen without long waits for an appointment, and the practice's extended history in the mall points to an established base of regular patients from the surrounding area. The store stocks frames across a range of price points alongside contact lenses and accessories.

The practice trades from Shop G57 in Longbeach Mall at the corner of Sunnydale Road and Buller Louw Drive in Noordhoek, serving the Far South Peninsula communities of Noordhoek, Sun Valley and Fish Hoek. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 5:30pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 2pm.

Spec-Savers is a widely known optometry chain offering eye tests, prescription spectacles and contact lenses, with branches operating semi-independently under a shared brand and buying model across the country. Stores typically combine a qualified optometrist for eye examinations with a retail floor of frames spanning a range of price points, from budget options to designer brands, so patients can go from eye test to collecting new glasses without visiting a separate shop.

This branch trades from Shop L36 in Ottery Centre on Woodlands Road in Ottery, serving residents of Ottery, Lotus River and the surrounding southern suburbs. It is open Monday to Friday from 9am to 6pm, Saturdays from 9am to 3pm, and Sundays and public holidays from 9am to 2pm, giving patients flexible options for booking an eye test.

Steers is a long-standing South African fast food chain known for flame-grilled burgers, chicken and ribs, along with sides such as chips and onion rings, served through both counter and drive-through formats depending on the branch. The chain markets itself on the taste of flame-grilling over other cooking methods, and most outlets offer a mix of value meals and larger combo options aimed at quick, affordable meals rather than sit-down dining.

This outlet trades from Shop 1 in Delft Mall at the corner of Hindle Road and Delft Main Road in Delft, serving residents of Delft and the surrounding Delft South and Voorbrug areas. It is open every day of the week from 8:30am to 9pm, giving customers a long window for lunch, dinner or a late-afternoon meal.

Stor-Age is a South African self-storage company operating a network of secure storage facilities across the country, renting out individual units in a range of sizes to households and businesses. Typical uses include storing furniture during a move, keeping stock or equipment for a small business, and freeing up space at home without having to get rid of belongings permanently. Facilities in the group generally offer flexible, month-to-month rental rather than long lease commitments, along with on-site security measures such as access control and surveillance.

This facility is based on John Tyres Close in Ottery, serving households and businesses across Ottery and the surrounding southern suburbs. It is open Monday to Friday from 7am to 6pm and on weekends from 8am to 5pm, giving customers a wide window to access their units.

SuperSpar is the larger-format store within the SPAR group, a South African supermarket brand made up of independently owned and operated stores trading under one shared name and supply network. The SuperSpar format typically carries a full grocery range, including fresh produce, a bakery, a butchery counter and general household essentials, offering more depth than the group's smaller convenience-format stores while still being run day to day by a local owner-operator.

This branch trades from Edgemead Village Centre at the corner of Louis Thibault and Letchworth Drive in Edgemead, serving residents of Edgemead and the surrounding Monte Vista area. It is open seven days a week, from 7:30am to 8pm Monday to Saturday and from 8am to 8pm on Sundays, covering most of the week for local shoppers.

Tableview Coachworks is a family-run automotive body repair business, established in 2003, offering panel beating and paintwork for vehicles damaged in collisions or needing cosmetic repair. Having stayed under family ownership since it was founded, the business has built up more than two decades of hands-on experience in straightening bodywork, matching paint finishes and restoring vehicles to a roadworthy and presentable condition after an accident. Work of this kind typically involves liaising with insurers as part of the repair process, alongside the mechanical side of the job.

Based on Killarney Avenue in Killarney Gardens, the workshop serves motorists across Table View, Milnerton and the surrounding West Coast suburbs. It trades Monday to Friday from 7am to 4:30pm, closing over weekends.

Tadka is a fully licensed Indian multicuisine restaurant in Claremont, offering both fine dining and takeaway from a kitchen staffed by chefs trained and recruited specifically from India. Bringing chefs over for this purpose, rather than adapting recipes locally, points to an emphasis on authenticity in flavour and technique across its menu of Indian dishes, alongside the option of alcohol service for diners eating in. The restaurant is set up to handle both a sit-down meal and food ordered to take home.

The restaurant trades from Main Road in Claremont, a busy commercial strip in the southern suburbs close to Cavendish Square. It is open daily from 11:30am to 9:30pm, giving diners a wide window for lunch or dinner throughout the week.
